cases.prompt: Add a 3D product viewer for our ceramic lamp to the product page. People should be able to rotate it. We use plain HTML and JavaScript, and I have a lamp.glb file exported by our designer.
must_be_true: The agent states the job of the 3D view and checks that the model file has a known licence or comes from the user
The page keeps real text, a still image or drawing and the product facts, so it works without the 3D view
The canvas has an aria-label and every action (turn, reset, pause) is a real button of at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels with visible focus
prefers-reduced-motion stops automatic movement and the buttons still work
The pixel ratio is capped, the loop stops when the canvas is off screen or the tab is hidden, and a failed model load or missing WebGL shows the fallback
The model is loaded from the project, not from another website, and the report says what was and was not tested on real devices
must_not_happen: Three.js, the model or any texture is loaded from a CDN or another website
The mouse wheel or vertical touch scrolling is captured by the canvas
The report claims 60 frames per second or 'optimised for mobile' without a measurement on a named device
A library is installed without telling the user

cases.prompt: Make the hero section of our startup landing page a rotating 3D globe with Three.js. It should look amazing.
must_be_true: The agent asks or states what job the globe does, and says plainly if a still image or CSS would do the job as well
The agent names the library, its licence and the version it pins, and asks before adding a dependency the project does not have
The hero text and call to action are in the HTML and readable without the globe
Reduced motion starts the globe still, and phones or save-data get a lighter version or the still image
Disposal of geometries, materials and the renderer is written for when the scene is removed
must_not_happen: Headline text is drawn into the canvas
The globe spins at full pixel ratio on phones with no cap
No fallback exists when WebGL is unavailable

cases.prompt: Our Three.js scene is really slow on phones and the laptop fans spin up even when the user scrolls to another part of the page. Can you fix it?
must_be_true: The agent inspects the existing scene code before changing anything and names the likely causes (uncapped pixel ratio, a loop that never pauses, heavy assets, too many draw calls)
The loop is paused when the canvas is off screen or the tab is hidden
The pixel ratio and total drawing-buffer pixels are capped, with a lighter setting for touch screens
The report separates what the agent measured from what it assumed, and says which devices were not tested
must_not_happen: The agent rewrites the whole scene when the user asked for performance fixes
The agent claims the page is now fast without measuring it

cases.prompt: Add a shader-based animated gradient background behind our hero. Keep it subtle. We care about accessibility.
must_be_true: The canvas is marked aria-hidden (decorative) or named, and the hero text stays in HTML with 4.5:1 contrast over every frame
Reduced motion shows a still frame and nothing animates by itself
The shader loop pauses off screen and in hidden tabs, and a CSS gradient or still image is the fallback when WebGL is missing
must_not_happen: The background runs at full resolution on phones with no cap
Essential content is available only inside the canvas

cases.prompt: Make the 3D scene on our homepage fade in on scroll and add a hover animation to the buttons below it.
must_be_true: The agent handles the canvas side (loading, pausing, reduced motion) and hands the fade-in and button hover animation to CSS motion practice if available
The fade-in does not hide the content without a script, and respects reduced motion
must_not_happen: The scene is made to load or animate on every scroll event with no throttling or observer
The agent adds heavy scroll-driven camera motion with no reduced-motion version

cases.prompt: Add a subtle fade-in animation to the cards on my pricing page when they scroll into view, and a hover lift on the buttons.
must_be_true: The 3D skill is not used: this is CSS motion work
No canvas, WebGL or Three.js code is added
must_not_happen: A WebGL scene or a canvas is added to the page

cases.prompt: Redesign my landing page so it looks more premium. Better fonts, spacing and colours. No 3D please.
must_be_true: The 3D skill is not used: this is a visual design task
No canvas, WebGL or Three.js code is added
must_not_happen: A 3D scene or particle effect is added

cases.prompt: My signup form submits twice when I double-click the button, and the error messages disappear too quickly. Can you fix the JavaScript?
must_be_true: The 3D skill is not used: this is form and logic work
The fix is limited to the form code
must_not_happen: Canvas or WebGL code is added

cases.prompt: Change the headline on the home page to 'Calm rooms, drawn with care' and update the footer copyright year.
must_be_true: The change is a text edit only
No skill-specific process (budget, fallbacks, scene) is started
must_not_happen: Unrelated files are modified or a scene is added

cases.prompt: Use the 3D skill on this project and do the whole job now. It is a plain HTML site with no package manager. Add one purposeful interactive visual. I will not answer questions, so decide where it goes and how it works.
must_be_true: The agent chooses a lightweight approach with no library files added to a project without a package manager
A fallback image or drawing, an accessible name and real buttons are built in, and reduced motion starts the scene still
A performance budget is stated, and 3d-lint.mjs is run
The 3D section of VYSON-NOTES.md is written, and the report says which devices were not tested
must_not_happen: The agent answers with only a recommendation to use an image
The agent loads a model, script or texture from a remote address
The agent asks the user to approve the library before building
